methodology.whatThisIs: A standing compilation of the static anchors UPSC has examined repeatedly over roughly twenty years, expressed as data so a tool can query it. An anchor is the syllabus concept that outlives the news event; a question is that anchor crossed with a current trigger and a directive verb.
methodology.frequencyEst: frequency_est is an editorial weight from 0-100 derived from the recurring-theme compilation, NOT a count of questions from a tagged corpus. It ranks anchors against each other for revision priority. It is not evidence about any single year.
methodology.recencyGapEst: recency_gap_est is an editorial 0-100 judgement of how overdue an anchor feels, where 100 means long absent and 0 means asked very recently. It is the weakest field here and the first that should be replaced with measured last-asked years.
methodology.stems: question_stems are written in authentic UPSC phrasing for answer-writing practice. They are practice prioritisation, never prediction. Nobody can tell you what will be asked.
methodology.facts: static_core names institutions, statutes and judgments only where the naming is settled. Every figure, percentage, ranking and award year is deliberately absent and pushed into the verify field instead, because a fluent wrong number written into a Mains answer costs marks silently.
methodology.howToMakeItReal: Tag the official papers from upsc.gov.in into the schema in the skill's pyq-pattern-decoder (§7), replace frequency_est with real counts and recency_gap_est with the actual last-asked year, then drop the provisional flag. That is the highest-value work available on this dataset and everything downstream improves the moment it exists.
methodology.conflicts: Where this file and the Union Public Service Commission disagree, the Commission is right.

bands.perennial: Appears in most cycles in some form. Floor competence here is not optional.
bands.high: Appears frequently and across papers. Worth a written answer, not just a note.
bands.medium: Periodic. Revise it, but do not build a month around it.
bands.emerging: A newer theme UPSC is still developing. Low history, high forward weight — new anchors tend to be asked again soon.

triggerTypes.EVENT: A dated occurrence — a summit, a launch, a crisis, a policy announcement.
triggerTypes.REPORT: An official report, survey, index or committee recommendation.
triggerTypes.JUDGMENT: A court decision, usually the Supreme Court.
triggerTypes.LEGISLATION: A bill, act, amendment, rule or notification.
triggerTypes.PERENNIAL: No trigger needed; the anchor is asked on its own terms.

papers.GS3: Economy, environment, science and technology, security

static_core: Constitutional guarantees run from Articles 14-16 through Article 15(3) permitting protective provisions
Legal capacity has expanded faster than social sanction, which is why reform and outcome diverge
Participation is not the same measure as remunerative work, and answers that conflate them lose the argument
anchors.prelims_angle: Constitutional and statutory provisions, the reservation legislation for legislatures, and which survey measures which indicator
traps: Writing only about the present when the marks sit in the movement from social reform to constitutional guarantee to contemporary gap
Treating women as a single category rather than one cut by caste, class and region
skeleton: Locate the phenomenon historically before describing it
Structural roots, present manifestation, regional variation, counter-current
Close on continuity and change, not on a call for awareness

stems.stem: Examine the extent to which legal reform has translated into substantive gender equality in India.
Discuss how the changing structure of employment has altered the position of women in Indian society.

verify: Current female labour force participation figures with the survey and round attached
The status and text of the legislature reservation legislation

static_core: The 74th Amendment listed municipal functions in the Twelfth Schedule but left transfer to state discretion
Urban failure is a devolution failure: functions, funds and functionaries move separately and rarely together
Planning capacity, not money, is usually the binding constraint on Indian cities
anchors.prelims_angle: The 74th Amendment machinery, Twelfth Schedule subjects, and the design of the major urban missions
traps: Listing problems of cities without naming who is constitutionally responsible for fixing them
Recommending a mission when the question asks about institutional capacity
skeleton: Quantify the shift, then name the governing institution
Design intent, actual functioning, the gap
Recommend an institutional change, not a scheme

stems.stem: Critically examine why the constitutional promise of the 74th Amendment has not produced empowered urban local bodies.
Discuss the relationship between unplanned urban growth and the increasing incidence of urban flooding in India.

verify: Current urban population share and its source
Which urban missions are active in the current cycle

static_core: Poverty measurement is contested by construction: a consumption line and a multidimensional index answer different questions
Growth reduces poverty through employment, and jobless growth breaks that link
Inequality of opportunity, not only of income, is what the Constitution's equality code addresses
anchors.prelims_angle: Which body publishes which measure, the dimensions of the multidimensional index, and the committee lineage of the poverty line
traps: Quoting a poverty figure without the measure, the year and the agency
Treating poverty and inequality as the same problem with the same remedy
skeleton: State which measure the answer is using and why
Causes, current policy response, the measurable gap
Sequence the way forward rather than listing schemes

stems.stem: Critically analyse the claim that a decline in measured poverty is compatible with rising inequality in India.
Discuss the limitations of consumption-based poverty measurement for policy design.

verify: The latest multidimensional poverty estimate with the publishing agency and year
Which consumption survey is currently the reference

static_core: Indian secularism is principled distance rather than strict separation, which is why the state legislates on religious practice
Articles 25-28 protect religious freedom subject to public order, morality and health
Regionalism is not automatically corrosive: it has produced both linguistic reorganisation and demands for separation
anchors.prelims_angle: The freedom of religion articles and their limits, the reorganisation timeline, and the constitutional provisions on minority institutions
traps: Arguing from sentiment where the question asks for a constitutional reading
Presenting regionalism as uniformly negative when the Constitution accommodated it deliberately
skeleton: Define the Indian variant against the textbook one
Constitutional design, judicial interpretation, contemporary strain
Close on the accommodation the Constitution actually chose

stems.stem: Examine how the Indian conception of secularism differs from the strict separation model, with reference to constitutional practice.
Comment on the view that regionalism has strengthened rather than weakened Indian federalism.

verify: Recent judgments on essential religious practices and their exact holdings

static_core: Globalisation reaches Indian society through labour markets, media and migration rather than through trade policy alone
It has loosened ascriptive hierarchy in some domains while sharpening inequality in others
Cultural change under globalisation is hybridisation, not replacement
anchors.prelims_angle: Institutional architecture of trade and its Indian obligations; diaspora policy instruments
traps: Writing an economics answer when the question is about society
Deciding globalisation is good or bad instead of showing what it changed and for whom
skeleton: Name the transmission channel before describing effects
One domain at a time: family, work, caste, gender, consumption
Close on hybridisation with a concrete example

stems.stem: Examine the effects of globalisation on the Indian family and on kinship obligations.
To what extent has globalisation weakened ascriptive hierarchies in Indian society?

verify: Current remittance and diaspora figures with source and year

static_core: India is in different phases of transition simultaneously, which is why a single national policy misfits most states
A demographic dividend is a window, not an endowment: it pays only through employment and skills
Ageing arrives before universal social security is built, which is the structural risk
anchors.prelims_angle: Transition stages, which survey reports fertility and mortality indicators, and the census and civil registration architecture
traps: Treating the dividend as automatic
Recommending population control where the data show fertility already at or below replacement
skeleton: Establish the regional divergence first
Window, conditions to convert it, consequences of missing it
Close on sequencing: skills and jobs before pensions

stems.stem: Examine the conditions under which India's demographic profile becomes a dividend rather than a burden.
Discuss the policy implications of the divergence in demographic transition across Indian states.

verify: Current total fertility rate by state with the survey round
Latest old-age dependency projection and its source

static_core: The movement's method changed with its social base: constitutional agitation, then mass mobilisation, then negotiation
Gandhian technique made a middle-class campaign into a mass one by attaching local grievance to national demand
Peasant, tribal and worker movements ran alongside the Congress-led struggle and were not always subordinate to it
anchors.prelims_angle: Chronology, session-and-resolution detail, personalities attached to specific movements, and press and legislation milestones
traps: Narrating events instead of assessing a claim about them
Reducing the struggle to a single leader or a single strand
skeleton: Take a position on the claim in the question in the first two lines
Phase by phase, with the social base of each
Include one non-Congress strand as counter-current

stems.stem: Evaluate the view that the Gandhian phase transformed the social base of the national movement rather than its aims.
Examine the role of tribal and peasant uprisings in shaping the anti-colonial struggle.

verify: Exact dates and resolutions where a question turns on them

static_core: Integration, reorganisation and land reform were one project: making a state capable of governing a diverse territory
Linguistic reorganisation accommodated identity rather than suppressing it, and that choice explains later stability
Land reform succeeded unevenly, and where it failed it shaped later agrarian politics
anchors.prelims_angle: Commission names and sequence, states created and when, and the components of land reform legislation
traps: Listing events without the state-building argument that connects them
Claiming land reform failed uniformly across India
skeleton: Frame it as a state-capacity problem
Integration, reorganisation, agrarian structure
Close on which choices are still load-bearing today

stems.stem: Evaluate the contribution of linguistic reorganisation to the stability of the Indian union.
Discuss why land reforms produced very different outcomes across Indian states.

verify: Commission names and the year of each reorganisation being cited

static_core: Architectural schools are distinguished by structure and plan, not by decoration, and answers should name the feature
The Bhakti and Sufi movements are social history as much as religious history
Heritage questions reward specific examples over general appreciation
anchors.prelims_angle: School-to-feature-to-site mapping, dynastic attribution, and the classification of dance and music traditions
traps: Praising instead of describing: an answer with no named feature or site scores as an appreciation
Missing the illustrate instruction, where examples are the body and not decoration
skeleton: One line locating the tradition in time and region
Feature, example, significance, repeated per point
A sketch where the question is architectural

stems.stem: Illustrate the distinguishing structural features of the major schools of Indian temple architecture.
Discuss the social significance of the Bhakti movement beyond its devotional content.

verify: Site names, dynastic attributions and inscription years before asserting them

static_core: The syllabus asks about processes and their consequences, not chronology for its own sake
Decolonisation left state boundaries that did not match nations, which is the origin of many current conflicts
Comparison across regions is what separates a strong answer from a summary
anchors.prelims_angle: Sequence of events, treaty names, and the institutional origins of the post-war order
traps: Answering Europe when the question says the world
Narrating a war rather than assessing its effect on the international order
skeleton: Name the process and its mechanism
Two regions compared, not one described
Close on the consequence still visible today

stems.stem: Examine how the process of decolonisation shaped the political geography of West Asia and Africa.
Discuss the consequences of the Industrial Revolution for colonised economies.

verify: Treaty names and dates where the answer turns on them

static_core: The monsoon is a large-scale circulation response to differential heating, modulated by ocean-atmosphere oscillations
Variability, not the mean, is what damages Indian agriculture
A mechanism question wants the process chain, and a diagram earns marks a paragraph cannot
anchors.prelims_angle: Mechanism terminology, oscillation names and their phases, and the geography of rainfall distribution
traps: Describing outcomes without the mechanism the verb asked for
Omitting the diagram in a physical geography answer
skeleton: State the mechanism in a chain of causes
Sketch it
Then the Indian consequence, quantified where sourced

stems.stem: Explain the mechanism of the Indian summer monsoon and the factors that modulate its interannual variability.
Discuss how increasing rainfall variability affects cropping decisions in India.

verify: Current oscillation phase and forecast source before citing this season

static_core: Hazard is physical, disaster is social: the same event produces different losses depending on exposure and capacity
Plate boundary type predicts the hazard signature of a region
Himalayan hazard is compounded by slope construction and drainage disruption, not only by seismicity
anchors.prelims_angle: Seismic zonation, boundary types and their landforms, and monitoring institutions
traps: Answering the event when the syllabus asks about the process or the response framework
Ignoring the human exposure half of the risk equation
skeleton: Process, then hazard signature, then exposure
One Indian region as the worked example
Close on mitigation that follows from the mechanism

stems.stem: Explain why the Himalayan region carries a compound hazard profile, and discuss the implications for construction norms.
Examine the relationship between plate boundary type and the hazards characteristic of a region.

verify: Seismic zone classifications and the current zonation source

static_core: Location follows the changing weight of inputs: raw material, then power, then market, then labour and logistics
Resource endowment without processing capacity exports value rather than capturing it
Critical mineral dependence is now a strategic question, not only an industrial one
anchors.prelims_angle: Mineral belt geography, industrial region names, and the institutions governing mineral allocation
traps: Listing locational factors without applying them to the industry in the question
Ignoring the strategic dimension when the trigger is a supply-chain event
skeleton: State which locational factor dominates for this industry and why
Then the Indian pattern, then the shift underway
Close on the policy lever that follows

stems.stem: Analyse how the determinants of industrial location have shifted in India over the past three decades.
Discuss the strategic implications of India's dependence on imported critical minerals.

verify: Import dependence figures for specific minerals with source and year

static_core: The Constitution treats caste disadvantage as a ground for protective provision, not as a category to be denied
Reservation jurisprudence has turned repeatedly on efficiency, creamy layer and the extent of permissible classification
Tribal disadvantage is territorial as well as social, which is why Fifth and Sixth Schedule governance exists
anchors.prelims_angle: The Schedules and their governance machinery, statutory commissions, and the legislative basis of protective provisions
traps: Debating reservation in the abstract when the question asks about a specific constitutional test
Collapsing tribal and caste disadvantage into one analysis
skeleton: Constitutional provision first, then the judicial test
Delivery record with a named institution
Close on the reform the jurisprudence points towards

stems.stem: Critically examine the constitutional tests that govern the extent of reservation in public employment.
Discuss why territorial protections for tribal areas require a different governance design from other social protections.

verify: Recent judgments on reservation limits and their exact holdings

static_core: Article 280 constitutes the Finance Commission, whose award sets both vertical and horizontal devolution
Cesses and surcharges sit outside the divisible pool, so the headline devolution share overstates what states receive untied
Article 279A's GST Council traded state rate autonomy for a common market, moving indirect taxation into a joint forum
anchors.prelims_angle: Finance Commission composition and mandate, what enters the divisible pool, GST Council design, and the difference between tied and untied transfers
traps: Writing about GST rates when the question asks about the allocation of power
Asserting a devolution percentage without naming the Commission and the year
skeleton: Open on the constitutional allocation, not on a definition of federalism
Design intent, actual functioning, the gap: one block each
Close with an institutional recommendation, not a plea for cooperation

stems.stem: Examine the extent to which the growth of cesses and surcharges has altered the substance of tax devolution in India.
Critically examine the claim that the GST Council represents cooperative federalism in practice.

verify: The current Commission's vertical devolution recommendation and the years it covers
GST Council voting weights and the majority required

static_core: Judicial review flows from Articles 13, 32 and 226 and was placed beyond amendment by the basic structure doctrine in Kesavananda Bharati
Public interest litigation widened standing, which expanded access and simultaneously invited the overreach charge
Proportionality is now the working standard for testing state action against rights, following Puttaswamy
anchors.prelims_angle: Writs and their scope, the amendment and appointment case lineage, and tribunal jurisdiction
traps: Omitting the verdict when the verb says critically examine
Treating activism and overreach as synonyms rather than as a question of institutional competence
skeleton: Constitutional source of the power in one line
Where review is legitimate, where it substitutes for the executive, and the test that distinguishes them
State a verdict with reasons

stems.stem: Critically examine the line between judicial review and judicial overreach in matters of policy.
Discuss how the proportionality standard has changed the review of executive action affecting fundamental rights.

verify: Case names and the exact proposition each judgment established before citing it

static_core: India adopts functional separation with deliberate overlap, so the test is encroachment on essential function rather than tidiness
The appointments question is about who guards independence, and every proposed alternative relocates rather than removes the problem
Discretionary offices, particularly the Governor's, are where the doctrine is tested most often in practice
anchors.prelims_angle: Appointment machinery for the higher judiciary, the Governor's discretionary powers, and the constitutional position of tribunals
traps: Describing the doctrine abstractly without the Indian variant
Recommending a commission without addressing why the previous design was struck down
skeleton: State the Indian variant, not Montesquieu
Institution by institution: where the friction actually occurs
Close on a reform that preserves independence and adds accountability

stems.stem: Examine the constitutional issues raised by the present system of appointment to the higher judiciary.
Critically examine the exercise of discretionary powers by Governors in the context of separation of powers.

verify: The current appointments procedure and the judgments that established it

static_core: Parliament's core function is scrutiny of the executive, and sitting days plus committee referral are the operative measures of it
Committees do the deliberative work the floor no longer has time for, which is why referral practice matters more than debate length
The Tenth Schedule's anti-defection design strengthened party control at the cost of individual deliberation
anchors.prelims_angle: Committee types and composition, money bill definition under Article 110, ordinance conditions, and Speaker's powers under the Tenth Schedule
traps: Lamenting disruption without measuring scrutiny
Citing sitting-day counts without a source and period
skeleton: Name the function being assessed before assessing it
Evidence of decline, institutional cause, the committee counterweight
Close on a procedural reform, not on an appeal to decorum

stems.stem: Critically examine the claim that the decline in legislative scrutiny is a procedural rather than a behavioural problem.
Evaluate the contribution of parliamentary committees to executive accountability in India.

verify: Sitting-day and bill-referral statistics with the source and the period they cover

static_core: The 73rd and 74th Amendments created the institutions and left the transfer of functions, funds and functionaries to state discretion
The Eleventh and Twelfth Schedules list subjects but do not compel devolution, which is the whole gap
State Finance Commissions are the constitutional mechanism for local resources and are the most ignored institution in the design
anchors.prelims_angle: Schedule contents, mandatory versus optional provisions, State Finance Commission mandate, and PESA's application to Fifth Schedule areas
traps: Praising the amendments and then complaining about outcomes without naming the discretion that connects them
Forgetting the fiscal leg: elections happen, money does not follow
skeleton: Constitutional design in two lines
Functions, funds, functionaries: assess each separately
Close on the State Finance Commission or on a statutory devolution mandate

stems.stem: Critically examine why three decades of constitutional status have not produced fiscally capable local governments.
Discuss the significance of PESA for tribal self-governance and the obstacles to its implementation.

verify: State Finance Commission constitution status across states

static_core: Independence is engineered through appointment, tenure, removal and funding, and a body is only as independent as the weakest of the four
Constitutional status (the CAG under Article 148, the Election Commission under Article 324, the UPSC under Article 315) confers protection that statutory bodies lack
A recommendatory mandate without a compliance mechanism produces reports rather than outcomes
anchors.prelims_angle: Which body is constitutional, statutory or executive; appointment and removal procedure; and the reporting line for each
traps: Confusing a statutory body with a constitutional one, which reverses the entire argument
Recommending more powers when the diagnosed problem is appointment or funding
skeleton: Mandate and constitutional or statutory basis
Independence tested on the four levers
Close on the specific lever that needs fixing

stems.stem: Examine the institutional safeguards that secure the independence of the Election Commission, and whether they remain adequate.
Evaluate the effectiveness of human rights institutions in India given their recommendatory mandate.

verify: Current appointment procedures, especially where recently amended by statute

static_core: The recurring problems are money, criminality and information asymmetry, and each has a different institutional fix
Transparency in political funding is the reform on which the others depend, because opacity protects the rest
Delimitation is a federal question as much as an electoral one, since it redistributes representation between states
anchors.prelims_angle: Disqualification grounds, the funding instruments and their statutory basis, and the Election Commission's powers under the model code
traps: Proposing state funding without engaging the enforcement problem it does not solve
Treating simultaneous elections as purely administrative when it has constitutional consequences
skeleton: Name the specific defect in the first line
One reform per paragraph, each with the institution that must act

stems.stem: Critically examine the reforms required to reduce the influence of undisclosed money in Indian elections.
Discuss the federal implications of a delimitation exercise based on current population.

verify: The current legal position on political funding instruments after recent judgments

static_core: Transparency is instrumental: it exists to make accountability possible, and an answer should show the causal link rather than assert the value
The Right to Information Act 2005 works through designated officers, timelines and an appellate commission; weakening any of the three weakens the whole
Proactive disclosure is cheaper and more effective than answering requests one at a time
anchors.prelims_angle: RTI machinery and exemptions, appellate structure, and the statutory basis of whistleblower and grievance mechanisms
traps: Arguing transparency as an end in itself
Ignoring the tension with privacy, which is where the marks are in a critically examine
skeleton: Link transparency to a named accountability outcome
Statutory machinery, then the failure point, then the counter-value
Close on proactive disclosure or on commission capacity

stems.stem: Examine how the right to information advances administrative accountability, and where it collides with the right to privacy.
Discuss the conditions under which social audit becomes an effective accountability instrument.

verify: Current pendency at information commissions with source

static_core: Digitisation changes the location of discretion rather than removing it, so accountability must be redesigned alongside it
Exclusion error is the characteristic failure of targeted digital delivery, and it is invisible in efficiency statistics
Back-end process reform is what makes a front-end portal work; without it the portal digitises the delay
anchors.prelims_angle: Architecture of the identity and payment stack, mission names and mandates, and the statutory basis of service guarantees
traps: Celebrating savings without addressing exclusion
Treating a portal as a reform when the process behind it is unchanged

Close on grievance redress and audit, not on more technology

stems.stem: Critically examine the claim that digital delivery has reduced discretion in Indian welfare administration.
Discuss the design safeguards needed to prevent exclusion in targeted benefit transfer.

verify: Savings and exclusion estimates for benefit transfer with the study and year attached

static_core: Scheme design fails at four predictable points: identification, entitlement, delivery and grievance
Rights-based statutes shift the default from discretion to entitlement, which is why the legislative form matters
Convergence between schemes, not the number of schemes, determines what a household actually receives
anchors.prelims_angle: Statutory basis of major entitlements, target group definitions, and the institutional machinery for each vulnerable group
traps: Listing schemes instead of evaluating a design feature
Writing about a group without the statute or commission that governs it
skeleton: State the entitlement and its legal basis
Test it at identification, delivery and grievance
Close on convergence or on a named institutional fix

stems.stem: Examine why rights-based welfare statutes have delivered better than scheme-based provision in some sectors and not in others.
Evaluate the adequacy of India's social security architecture for informal workers.

verify: Coverage and outlay figures for any scheme named, with the year and the ministry

static_core: Both sectors are state subjects funded largely by the centre, which is why capacity varies more than policy does
Health spending is judged by out-of-pocket burden, not by insurance enrolment
In education the binding constraint has moved from access to learning outcome, and the policy instruments have not fully followed
anchors.prelims_angle: Constitutional placement, the statutory right to education, insurance and mission architecture, and which survey measures learning
traps: Confusing insurance coverage with access to care
Recommending higher spending without naming what the money buys
skeleton: Quantify the outcome gap, then name who is constitutionally responsible
Financing, provision, regulation, workforce
Close on primary care or on teacher capacity, whichever the question invites

stems.stem: Critically examine why increased health insurance coverage has not reduced out-of-pocket expenditure proportionately in India.
Examine the shift from access to learning outcomes in Indian school education and its policy implications.

verify: Health expenditure as a share of GDP and out-of-pocket share, with the account and year

static_core: The service was designed for order and now must deliver outcomes, and most reform debates are versions of that mismatch
Neutrality and responsiveness pull in opposite directions, and the officer's problem is the boundary between them
Domain expertise, performance appraisal and tenure security are three separate reforms often argued as one
anchors.prelims_angle: Constitutional protections for services, recruitment machinery, and the recommendations of the major administrative reform commissions

stems.stem: Critically examine the tension between political neutrality and responsiveness in the Indian civil service.
Discuss whether domain specialisation can be built within the existing structure of the civil services.

verify: Reform commission recommendations quoted, with the commission and report number

static_core: Neighbourhood policy is asymmetry management: India is larger than every neighbour, and that fact drives their hedging
The reliable analytical frame is political, economic, strategic, cultural and multilateral, then convergences and frictions
Connectivity and delivery record matter more than declaratory policy in this region
anchors.prelims_angle: Treaty and agreement names, connectivity project geography, and grouping membership
traps: Writing sentiment instead of interest
Assessing a bilateral relationship without the third-party factor that actually shapes it

static_core: Post-war institutions encode a distribution of power that no longer exists, which is the structural case for reform and the reason it stalls
India's approach is plurilateral hedging: several overlapping groupings rather than one alignment
Reform demands are credible only when paired with a willingness to accept obligations
